<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;2, 2025, YPF signed a Memorandum of Understanding (&#147;MOU&#148;) with the Province of Santa Cruz and Fomicruz S.E. (&#147;Fomicruz&#148;)
for the purpose of establishing the general terms and conditions upon which the assignment by YPF to Fomicruz of the exploitation concessions &#147;Cerro Piedra - Cerro Guadal Norte&#148;, &#147;Barranca Yankowsky&#148;, &#147;Los Monos&#148;,
&#147;El Guadal - Lomas del Cuy&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Vasco&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Yatel&#148;, &#147;Pico Truncado - El Cord&oacute;n&#148;, &#147;Los Perales - Las Mesetas&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Le&oacute;n -

and the issuance of the corresponding decree by the Province of Santa Cruz, was approved by YPF&#146;s Board of Directors on April&nbsp;9, 2025 and Decree No.&nbsp;376/2025 was issued by the Province of Santa Cruz on May&nbsp;6, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;2, 2025, YPF and Fomicruz signed an assignment agreement for the transfer of 100% of the participating interest in the aforementioned
exploitation and transportation concessions. The transfer was approved by Decree No.&nbsp;539/2025 published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Santa Cruz on June&nbsp;18, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;19, 2025, YPF and Fomicruz executed the notarial deed, thereby formalizing and perfecting the aforementioned assignment. Additionally, YPF
and Fomicruz signed a transitory operation agreement for all the assigned exploitation concessions, pursuant to which YPF shall continue to operate said concessions for a maximum period of up to 6 months. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assignment agreements that have met the agreed closing conditions as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial

their sale at the end of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2025, and therefore these groups of assets continue to be classified as held for sale as of that date. </P>

June&nbsp;4, 2025 YPF signed an assignment agreement to transfer its 7.1960% participating interest in &#147;El Tordillo&#148;, &#147;Puesto Quiroga&#148; and &#147;La Tapera&#148; exploitation concessions and the transportation concessions
associated with such exploitation concessions, in favor of Crown Point Energ&iacute;a S.A. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the assignment agreement is subject to the fulfillment of closing
conditions, including the formal resolution by the corresponding enforcement authorities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Restinga Al&iacute;</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;19, 2025 YPF signed an agreement that establishes the terms and conditions for the reversion of the &#147;Restinga Al&iacute;&#148;
exploitation concession, located in the Province of Chubut. On July&nbsp;24, 2025 the Legislature of the Province of Chubut approved the agreement through Law XVII No.&nbsp;162/2025, which was enacted on August&nbsp;1, 2025, and is pending its
publication in the corresponding Official Gazette. Additionally, as of the issuance date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the reversion agreement is subject to the approval by decree of the Executive Branch of the
Province of Chubut. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company has signed assignment
agreements for certain groups of assets as held for sale that are subject to closing conditions mainly related to regulatory and provincial approvals, for which the Company is taking the necessary steps to close; and it is highly probable that these
assets will be disposed. In addition, the Company maintains groups of assets as held for sale for which agreements have not yet been signed but continues in negotiations with third parties for their disposal or reversal. The delay in the fulfillment
of the plan for the disposal of mature fields is due to the complexity of the negotiations, which is beyond the Company&#146;s control. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company considers
that the disposal of such assets continues to be highly probable during 2025. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:11pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Considering that the assets classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell (&#147;fair
value&#148;), the Company evaluates the changes in fair value, recognizing a profit up to the limit of the impairment loss previously recognized or an impairment loss in addition to that previously recognized for such changes, (see Note 2.b.13) to
the annual consolidated financial statements). The carrying amount of the assets held for sale and associated liabilities may be adjusted in future periods depending on the results of the disposal process carry out by YPF and the economic
consideration to be agreed with third parties for such assets. </P>

income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the effective income tax rate expected as of the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, considering the tax criteria that the
Group assumes to apply during the fiscal year. If the estimate of such rate is modified based on new elements of judgment, the income tax expense could require adjustments in subsequent periods. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2025, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,922 and treasury shares amount to 11 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares of
common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2025, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the affirmative
vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s exploitation and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the voluntary
dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the outstanding
Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, the Company has not repurchased any of its own shares. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, the General Shareholders&#146; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF (see Note 2.b))
corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2024 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings: (i)&nbsp;completely release the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments;
(ii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 34,205 to appropriate a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 6,787,343 to appropriate a reserve for investments. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="otv10518_100"></A>35. CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENTS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.a) Exploitation concessions, transport concessions and exploration permits </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The most relevant agreements of exploitation concessions, transport concessions and exploration permits that took place in the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2024 are described in Note 35.a) to the annual consolidated financial statements. Updates for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Hydrocarbon Unconventional Exploitation Concessions (&#147;CENCH&#148;, by its acronym in Spanish) in the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;10, 2025, by means of Decrees No.&nbsp;275/2025, 276/2025 and 277/2025 the Executive Branch of the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n approved the
granting of the CENCH in the &#147;Aguada de la Arena&#148;, &#147;La Angostura Sur I&#148; and &#147;La Angostura Sur II&#148;, and &#147;Narambuena&#148; blocks, respectively. These CENCH have the following characteristics: </P>

subsidiary Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas under such agreements. In addition, related to the 25% equity interest of Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas in SESA, on May&nbsp;30, 2025 the Company granted a guarantee in favor of Golar Hilli

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.d) Regulations applicable to the New Energies business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.c.3), 36.c.5) and 36.c.6) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.d.1) Regulatory requirements applicable to natural gas
distribution </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Tariff schemes and tariff renegotiations </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">ENARGAS, through several resolutions, approved the transition tariff schemes to be applied by Metrogas until the rates resulting from the RQT came into
force in accordance with the provisions of Decree No.&nbsp;55/2023. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;257/2025 was published, which
approved: (i)&nbsp;the RQT corresponding to Metrogas; (ii)&nbsp;the segmentation of residential users; (iii)&nbsp;the investment plans for the five-year period 2025 - 2030; and (iv)&nbsp;the initial tariff scheme and the schemes of rates and charges
corresponding to Metrogas effective as from May&nbsp;1, 2025. The increase expected as a result of the RQT process will be effective in 31 consecutive monthly increases, which recognizes a cost for the deferral at a real weighted average cost of the
capital employed rate in pesos of 7.64% and establishes that the increase in distribution tariffs for May 2025 applicable to residential users and general service customers will be 3%. The application of the remaining increase derived from the RQT
will be completed in the remaining 30 installments, plus the recognition of the cost of the aforementioned deferral. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;5, 2025, SE
Resolution No.&nbsp;241/2025 was published, which established that the transportation and distribution tariffs will be adjusted on a monthly basis according to the variations in the indexes established by ENARGAS in the RQT, which correspond to the
variation in equal parts of the IPC and the Internal Wholesale Price Index (&#147;IPIM&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) published by the INDEC. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
June&nbsp;6, 2025, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;363/2025 was published, which approved: (i)&nbsp;the methodology for the monthly adjustment of tariffs; and (ii)&nbsp;the tariff charts to be applied by Metrogas effective as from June&nbsp;6, 2025.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">ENARGAS, through several resolutions, approved the tariff schemes to be applied by Metrogas on a monthly basis within the framework of the RQT in
accordance with the provisions of ENARGAS Resolution No. 363/2025.<U>Procedure for the compensation of the lower revenues received by natural gas distributors from their users</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;24/2025 repealed as from February&nbsp;1, 2025 MINEM Resolution No.
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">508-E/2017,</FONT> which established the procedure to compensate natural gas distributors for lower revenues due to benefits and/or bonuses and higher costs of UNG and unified the compensation mechanisms for lower
revenues received as a consequence of the application of incentive programs involving bonuses on the price of natural gas in the PIST. The amounts to be compensated will be deducted from the amounts to be paid by distributors to natural gas
producers and will be directly compensated by the SE through the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.d.2) Regulatory framework associated with electric power generation </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;7, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;450/2025 was published, which approves the following amendments to the Regulatory Framework associated with electric
power generation: (i)&nbsp;maximum competition and free contracting is guaranteed to generators; (ii)&nbsp;supply contracts will be freely negotiated between the parties; (iii)&nbsp;the figure of &#147;storer&#148; is introduced as the owner of
energy storage facilities; (iv)&nbsp;the figure of &#147;free user&#148; is introduced, who, together with large users, may contract independently and for own consumption the energy supply; (v)&nbsp;allows the PEN to authorize generators,
distributors and/or large users to build, at their exclusive cost and to satisfy their own needs, a line and/or extension of the transmission grid, which will not provide a public transportation service; and (vi)&nbsp;the extensions of the Argentine
Electricity Grid (&#147;SADI&#148;, by its acronym in Spanish) may be of free initiative and at the own risk of whoever executes them. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>CAMMESA </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through complementary notes to SE Resolution No.&nbsp;21/2025, informed to CAMMESA of the &#147;Guidelines for the Standardization of the MEM and
its Progressive Adaptation&#148;, which detail the modifications foreseen for the management of fuels, the determination of prices and the operation of the term market and the spot market are detailed. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.d.3) Decree No.&nbsp;55/2023 &#147;Emergency in the National Energy Sector&#148; </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;2, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;370/2025 was published extending the emergency of the national energy sector until July&nbsp;9, 2026. It also
provided for the extension of the intervention of ENRE and ENARGAS until July&nbsp;9, 2026 or until the constitution, commencement and appointment of the members of the Board of Directors of the National Gas and Electricity Regulatory Agency. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;7, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;452/2025 was published, establishing the National Gas and Electricity Regulatory Agency and granting a term of 180
days for its commencement of operations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.e) Incentive programs for hydrocarbon production </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.d) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended June&nbsp;30, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.e.1) Incentive programs for natural gas production
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Plan for Reinsurance and Promotion of Federal Hydrocarbon Production Domestic Self-Sufficiency, Exports, Imports Substitution and the
Expansion of the Transportation System for all Hydrocarbon Basins in the Country 2023-2028 (&#147;Plan GasAr 2023-2028&#148;)</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through
several resolutions, approves the natural gas prices at the PIST to be passed-through to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">end-users</FONT> in connection with current contracts entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through complementary notes to SE Resolution No.&nbsp;21/2025, instructed CAMMESA to apply a new order of priority for the dispatch of natural gas
and established that the acquisition of fuels will be carried out through 2 modalities: (i)&nbsp;auctions by CAMMESA for the purchase of spot volumes; and (ii)&nbsp;bids by which generators auction volumes with a maximum reference price based on
round 4.2. of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;11, 2025, the Argentine Government announced measures to loosen the foreign exchange
regime and reinforce the monetary framework. By virtue of this, the BCRA implemented a new foreign exchange regime in which certain restrictions to access the Foreign Exchange Market were eliminated. The following are the main measures: (i)&nbsp;the
&#147;crawling peg&#148; adjustment mechanism is eliminated and the dollar exchange rate in the Foreign Exchange Market may fluctuate in a range between 1,000 pesos and 1,400 pesos, whose limits will be increased at a rate of 1% per month;
(ii)&nbsp;the &#147;blend&#148; dollar was eliminated (see Note 36.i) &#147;Export Increase Program&#148; section); (iii) certain foreign exchange restrictions to individuals for the purchase of foreign currency were eliminated; (iv)&nbsp;access to
the Foreign Exchange Market is allowed without prior approval of the BCRA for the payment of dividends to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-resident</FONT> shareholders accrued as from fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2025; and
(v)&nbsp;the terms for the payment of foreign trade transactions are flexibilized, eliminating the schedule established by the BCRA for access to the Foreign Exchange Market without prior approval for the payment of imports of goods with customs
entry registration as from December&nbsp;13, 2023 and of services rendered and/or accrued as from such date. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Export Increase Program </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;14, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;269/2025 repealed the Export Increase Program and as from such date the proceeds from the export of goods and
services, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-export</FONT> financings, post- export financings and advance payments must be settled 100% through the Foreign Exchange Market within a general term of 20 days. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.l) CNV regulatory framework </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Information requirements as Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company is registered in the CNV under the category
&#147;Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent - Direct Participant&#148;, record No.&nbsp;549. Considering the Company&#146;s business and the CNV Rules, the Company will not, under any circumstance, offer brokerage services to third parties
for transactions in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV, and it will also not open operating accounts to third parties to issue orders and trade in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with the CNV Rules, the Company is subject to the provisions of Article 5 c), Chapter II, Title VII of the CNV Rules, &#147;Settlement and
Clearing Agent - Direct Participant&#148;. In this respect, as set forth in Article 13, Chapter II, Title VII, of the CNV Rules, as of June&nbsp;30, 2025, the equity of the Company exceeds the minimum equity required by such Rules, which amounts to
714. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Additional and/or complementary information </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">According to the dispositions established in Article 3, item 7, section d), Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV rules relating to the disclosure requirement
of unpaid accrued dividends on preferred shares, we inform that the Company has not issued any preferred shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">According to the dispositions
established in Article 3, item 7, section e), Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV rules relating to the disclosure requirement of the conditions, circumstances and deadlines for the cessation of restrictions to the distribution of unappropriated
retained earnings and losses and/or reserves, we inform that the restrictions to the distribution of unappropriated retained earnings and losses and/or reserves are detailed in Note 31 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with the limits set forth in Article 31 of the LGS and in accordance with the provisions of Article 6, Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV
regulations, we inform those investments in other companies, excluding those with complementary or integrating corporate purpose, do not exceed such limits. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="otv10518_103"></A>38. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 38 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and
similar obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 2,802 and 1,680 for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended
June&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Short-term benefit programs</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the short-term benefit programs was 99,253 and 86,072 for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT>
periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of June&nbsp;30, 2025, there are 4.6&nbsp;million number of PSARs outstanding with and a weighted average fair value of US$ 17.24 per PSARs. The amount
charged to expense in relation with Value Generation Plan was 1,116 and 2.162 for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December&nbsp;31, 2024, weighted average fair
value was US$ 28.6 per PSARs. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the remaining share-based benefit plans was 5,824 and 1,986 to be
settled in equity instruments, for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and 8,265 to be settled in cash, for the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">six-month</FONT> period ended
June&nbsp;30, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 2.b.11) to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the accounting policies for share-based benefit plans.
Repurchases of treasury shares are disclosed in Note 32. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="otv10518_105"></A>40. SUBSEQUENT EVENTS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Vaca Muerta Sur Project guarantee</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
July&nbsp;8, 2025, our associated VMOS signed an international syndicated loan for US$ 2.000&nbsp;million to finance the construction of the Vaca Muerta Sur Project. As guarantee for the obligations assumed in this loan, VMOS&#146;s shareholders,
including YPF, have granted a fiduciary assignment of their VMOS&#146;s shares as collateral for such financing, which will remain in force until the completion of the project. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Issuance of NO</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;22, 2025, the
Company issued in the local market Class&nbsp;XXXVIII and Class&nbsp;XXXIX NO for a nominal amount of US$ 250&nbsp;million maturing in July 2027 and US$ 167&nbsp;million maturing in July 2030, respectively. Class&nbsp;XXXVIII NO accrue and pay
interest quarterly at a fixed annual nominal rate of 7.5% and Class&nbsp;XXXIX NO accrue and pay interest semiannually at a fixed annual nominal rate of 8.75%. The integration of Class&nbsp;XXXVIII NO was made in kind with (i)&nbsp;Class&nbsp;XXV NO
for US$ 50&nbsp;million, (ii)&nbsp;Class&nbsp;XXIX NO for US$ 47&nbsp;million, and (iii)&nbsp;Class&nbsp;XXXVI NO for US$ 3&nbsp;million, the remaining amount was integrated in cash. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Acquisition of Vaca Muerta Inversiones S.A.U.</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;6, 2025, YPF entered into a share purchase agreement (the &#147;Agreement&#148;) with Total Austral S.A. whereby, subject to the
fulfillment of closing conditions set forth in the Agreement, YPF will acquire 100% of the shares and capital stock of Vaca Muerta Inversiones S.A.U. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount of the transaction is US$ 500&nbsp;million, subject to adjustments based on the cash flows of Vaca Muerta Inversiones S.A.U. between January
2025 and the closing date of the transaction. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">If all the closing conditions set forth in the Agreement are fulfilled, YPF will become the sole owner
and shareholder of 100% of capital stock of Vaca Muerta Inversiones S.A.U., which will hold a 45% working interest in the La Escalonada and Rinc&oacute;n La Ceniza unconventional exploitation concessions in the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, there have been no other significant subsequent events whose
effect on Group&#146;s financial position, results of operations or their disclosure in notes to the financial statements for the period ended as of June&nbsp;30, 2025, should have been considered in said financial statements under IFRS. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors&#146; meeting and authorized to be issued on
August&nbsp;7, 2025. </P>
